thread.title_full: German carmakers threatened by fallout from Nexperia chip supply halt - NewsBreak

author: DPA
title: German carmakers threatened by fallout from Nexperia chip supply halt - NewsBreak
text:
By DPA ,
4 hours ago
German car manufacturers were on Wednesday dealing with the fallout from the interruption in supply at Dutch chip manufacturer Nexperia, as the government in Berlin joined the effort to find a solution as fast as possible.
While Mercedes-Benz does not expect any short-term disruptions, Volkswagen is not ruling out short-term production restrictions.
The chairman of the German Electro and Digital Industry Association (ZVEI), Wolfgang Weber, told dpa that member companies were looking for alternative suppliers. One division of the association is dedicated to the automotive industry.
Although there were hopeful signs, Weber said, it was unclear how suitable the replacement components would be.
"We cannot give the all-clear yet," he said, adding that the crisis must be resolved quickly at the political level.
Volkswagen said on Wednesday that "currently, production is unaffected. However, given the dynamic situation, impacts on production in the short term cannot be ruled out."
Volkswagen is already in discussions with the Federal Employment Agency about potentially placing several tens of thousands of employees on the subsidized furlough scheme known as short-time work. The company did respond to a request to comment on the possibility.
Thanks to good cooperation with suppliers and lessons learned from the chip crisis, Mercedes-Benz is "secured in the short-term period," the company said on Wednesday in response to a request from dpa. "We are working intensively with our partners to close any potential gaps that may arise."
Reliable forecasts are difficult to make at this point in time, the carmaker said.
Supply problem has deeper roots
Nexperia is experiencing supply problems after the Dutch government took control of the company, which was previously managed by a Chinese parent corporation.
In response, China halted the export of Nexperia products, such as chips for the automotive industry.
The German Association of the Automotive Industry (VDA) warned on Tuesday of potential disruptions due to the issues at Nexperia, including production stoppages.
The German government is also looking for solutions.
A spokesperson for the Economy Ministry in Berlin said that the ministry was concerned and was in close dialogue with the various parties involved, including the Chinese government.
The ministry was set to hold a meeting with associations and companies from the automotive and electronics industries on the crisis at Nexperia later Wednesday, dpa learnt.
No easy switch
At first glance, these are mass-produced goods, said Peter Fintl, automotive expert at IT service provider Capgemini.
However, they are often highly customized and therefore not so easy to replace. “For certain components, you can't just switch to other manufacturers,” he said.
This makes the search for replacement suppliers complicated and time-consuming, he argued. Changes to supply chains are possible in principle, “however, we're not talking about days or weeks here, but months or quarters," he said.
